clue.text: What could deliver intensive care to all, with twice hospital area?

definitions.text: What could deliver intensive care to all, with twice hospital area?

indicators.note: what could deliver these letters is a fresh arrangement of them, so they are reworked
twice asks for the hospital letter to be used two times over

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: A question about what kind of system could bring intensive care to everyone, given double the hospital space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could deliver' signals an anagram of INTENSIVE CARE TO ALL plus H, H and A; the whole clue also describes Britain's state-funded health system.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's state-run health system was founded to offer medical treatment, including intensive care, free to every citizen.

clue.text: Greeting that's not touching is a risk, potentially

indicators.note: potentially suggests these letters could become something else when rearranged

explanation.surface: Greeting someone without contact is warned to carry a hazard.
explanation.definitionFit: A kiss blown or made near the cheek is a salutation in which lips never meet skin.

clue.text: One medium flotation losing 20% over year by following models?

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
M is the clothing-size abbreviation for medium

indicators.note: in a down clue over means the letters are turned upside down, read backwards
losing says letters go missing from the flotation word; the 20% fixes how many, a fifth of ten

parts.note: levitation is floating in the air, a kind of flotation

explanation.surface: A financial puzzle about a share flotation losing a fifth of its value over a year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing 20%' drops ON, two of the ten letters, from LEVITATION; 'over' turns LEVITATI into ITATIVEL. 'flotation' wants to be a stock-market launch; it is floating in the air.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting imitatively means copying, doing things after the example of others.

clue.text: Relative newcomer is exposing council estate's leaders

indicators.note: leaders are the front letters of each of the preceding words

explanation.surface: A new arrival is revealing the heads of a housing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: A brother's or sister's daughter is a family member.

clue.text: For Parisians, the standard desire is ultimately desperate

parts.note: la is French for the, as Parisians would say it
an itch is a restless craving or desire

explanation.surface: A French flag carries the longing for something in the end hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For Parisians, the' asks for the French feminine article.
explanation.definitionFit: A final, all-out effort made when everything else has failed is a desperate one at the very end.

clue.text: Serious type of rock held by the mob

indicators.note: held by says the answer sits inside the following words, spanning them

explanation.surface: A gang of criminals harbours an earnest musician.
explanation.definitionFit: This emotional, confessional strain of punk is known for its earnestness.

clue.text: A propeller encased in timber is not working

indicators.note: encased in puts the first pieces inside the timber word

parts.note: a log is a piece of timber
a fish's fin propels it through water

explanation.surface: An idle ship's propeller sits wrapped in wood.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazing about idly means doing no work at all.

clue.text: Saunter into eyeshot's rendered assistance for server

indicators.note: into places the saunter word inside the jumbled letters
rendered here means made into something new, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: to stroll is to saunter

explanation.surface: Someone wanders into view to help a waiter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rendered' rearranges the letters of 'eyeshot's' to make HOSTESEY. 'Saunter' looks like the surface verb but supplies the inserted piece.
explanation.definitionFit: This wheeled serving cart with warming compartments helps whoever dishes up a meal.

clue.text: Terrible sore throat? That's a degenerative condition

indicators.note: terrible suggests something mangled, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: that's expands to it is

explanation.surface: A bad throat infection turns out to be a chronic disorder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Terrible' rearranges SORE THROAT plus ITIS (from 'That's' read as 'it is').
explanation.definitionFit: A wearing-down of cartilage in the joints, this disease worsens with age.

clue.text: See 1
Campaign messages without diary parts

indicators.note: parts means the without word splits open to let the diary word in

parts.note: sans is a literary word for without
a log is a daily record or diary

explanation.surface: A campaign issues statements with no extracts from a journal.
explanation.definitionFit: Catchy phrases used in political or advertising drives are mottoes.

clue.text: Priest with life-giving drink getting half-cut

indicators.note: half-cut here means the word loses half of its letters

parts.note: an elixir is a potion supposed to give life

explanation.surface: A clergyman takes a restorative drink and gets tipsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' is British slang for drunk, but here it removes the last three of six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, the priest at Shiloh brought up the young Samuel.

clue.text: Early male trouble, foot covered by pointed cut

indicators.note: covered by puts the first pieces inside the pointed word
cut means the pointed word loses its final letter

parts.note: to have pointed a weapon is to have aimed it
he is the male pronoun
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: A man has an early problem with his foot covered by a sharp gash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims AIMED to AIME, and 'covered by' puts HEADOFT inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in advance of the scheduled moment means arriving sooner than expected.

clue.text: Following hit, young male soldiers possibly make for tropical trees

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit
a boy is a young male
soldier ants are a caste of ant, so ants may be soldiers

explanation.surface: After a strike, young troops head for the palms.
explanation.definitionFit: Flame trees with vivid red flowers grow across the warm regions near the equator.

clue.text: How someone virtuous collars Louisiana mugger, say

parts.note: as can mean how, in the way that

indicators.note: collars means grabs round, so the outer pieces enclose the state letters

parts.note: a saint is a virtuous person
LA is the postal abbreviation for Louisiana

explanation.surface: A good person grabs a mugger in Louisiana.
explanation.definitionFit: A mugger is one example of an attacker who sets upon a victim.

clue.text: Order ship to turn to left in task for course

indicators.note: order here is the command that sets the change in motion
to turn to says one set of letters is changed into another

parts.note: an assignment is a task
SS is the abbreviation for steamship

explanation.surface: A captain is told to steer to port while on a mission.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Order ... to turn to' signals the letter swap within the task word. 'course' here is a route, as in the alignment of a road or railway, not a meal or a class.
explanation.definitionFit: The planned route of a road or railway is its line, as surveyors call it.

clue.text: Answer to name but one lives for sponsorship

parts.note: e.g. introduces a single example
is can mean exists or lives

explanation.surface: Answering by naming one person who supports the cause.
explanation.definitionFit: Under the protection or backing of someone means under their patronage.

clue.text: Wind energy's double to start with

indicators.note: to start with puts the double word at the front, before the energy letter

parts.note: a twin is a double
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Wind power is twice as strong at the outset.
explanation.definitionFit: To twist or coil string round something is to wrap it.

clue.text: With the opening cut, Kill Bill shows malevolence

indicators.note: with its opening cut, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: taken as written
Bill and Will are both pet forms of William

explanation.surface: A film title, trimmed, reveals hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kill Bill' is the title of a Quentin Tarantino film.
explanation.definitionFit: Spite or hostility towards others is wishing them harm.

clue.text: Breaking in half of steeds, one part of bridle provides restraint

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: breaking means bursting into, so the later pieces go inside
half of keeps only the front three of six letters

parts.note: horses are steeds
one is the Roman numeral I
the bit is the mouthpiece of a bridle

explanation.surface: Breaking in horses, a bridle piece holds them back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half of' keeps HOR from HORSES; 'Breaking' looks like the start of 'breaking in' horses, but it is the container signal, with 'in' a separate piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that checks or slows a process acts as a curb.

clue.text: Cheat on Exercise 6 with twit

indicators.note: to exercise is to put through movements, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the answer to 6 down is a word for a serious rock fan

explanation.surface: A fitness instruction involving a fool.
explanation.walkthrough: '6' refers to the answer of 6 down, EMO.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unfaithful to a partner by seeing someone else is deceiving them.

clue.text: Call to support partner in phone credit before day's end

indicators.note: in places the partner word inside the phone word

parts.note: to ring someone is to phone them
an ally is a partner
CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: end picks the final letter of the day word

explanation.surface: A partner has phone credit before the close of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A slogan or shout that rouses people to back a cause is a battle cry.

clue.text: What sounds like "sowing machine" and may have needles?

indicators.note: what sounds like says the word is heard, not seen

parts.note: a seeder is a machine for sowing

explanation.surface: A riddle about a farm machine that might also have needles like a sewing machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sowing machine' plays on 'sewing machine', which also has needles.
explanation.definitionFit: This evergreen conifer bears needle-like leaves.

clue.text: Night person regularly featured by Boswell

indicators.note: regularly takes every other letter of the following name

explanation.surface: Someone who stays up late features often in Boswell's writing.
explanation.walkthrough: James Boswell was Samuel Johnson's biographer.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who stays up late is likened to the nocturnal bird.

clue.text: Ventures almost a decade in Adriatic port

parts.note: tries are attempts or ventures

indicators.note: almost drops the last letter of the decade word

parts.note: a decade is ten years

explanation.surface: Business ventures spend nearly ten years in a seaport.
explanation.definitionFit: This north-eastern Italian city is a harbour on the Adriatic sea.

clue.text: Runner's jump falling short

indicators.note: falling short drops the last letter of the jump word

parts.note: to skip is to jump

explanation.surface: An athlete leaps but doesn't make the distance.
explanation.definitionFit: A ski is a long narrow runner on snow; the 's stands for is.

clue.text: Study spike which forms tooth

parts.note: a den is a private room or study
a tine is a prong or spike

explanation.surface: Researching a sharp point that makes up a tooth.
explanation.definitionFit: The hard calcareous tissue under enamel makes up the bulk of each tooth.

clue.text: Second delicate note was still lacking regard for others

parts.note: elfin means small and delicate
te is a note of the sol-fa scale
to have rested is to have stayed still

explanation.surface: A delicate second note remained without consideration for others.
explanation.definitionFit: Being concerned only with one's own advantage means ignoring other people.
